Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

qte 2.1.0 (development version)

Breaking changes

  • Removed the deprecated two-period functions, as announced in 2.0.0: CiC(), QDiD(), MDiD(), ddid2(), panel.qtet(), ci.qte(), ci.qtet() and ggqte(). Use cic(), qdid(), mdid(), ddid(), panel_qtt(), unc_qte() (with target = "qtt" for the QTT; lou_qtt() for staggered adoption) and autoplot() instead.
  • Removed the exported helper panelize.data(), which only served those functions.
  • Removed the exported internal QTEparams() parameter container. unc_qte() now has self-contained estimation and bootstrap code and no longer uses it.
  • formula.tools, data.table and parallel are no longer dependencies.
  • Requires ptetools (>= 1.1.0) and BMisc (>= 1.4.11).
  • unc_qte()’s covariate argument xformla is renamed xformula, matching the other estimators. xformla still works for now, with a deprecation warning. The new clustervars argument comes right after weightsname, so calls passing probs or later arguments by position need updating.
  • est_method = "or" (outcome regression) in unc_qte() and lou_qtt() is renamed "reg", the name did uses, and the name in the new cdf_did(). "or" still works, with a deprecation warning.

New features

  • cic(), ddid(), qdid(), mdid(), lou_qtt() and panel_qtt() gain a clustervars argument, as in did::att_gt(), to cluster standard errors at a level above the unit (ptetools #6). With the empirical bootstrap, whole clusters are resampled.

  • unc_qte() also gains clustervars: its bootstrap then resamples whole clusters instead of rows.

  • QTT results (gt_type = "qtt") from the panel estimators now also carry the ATT, aggregated with the same weights as the QTT, and the curve QTT(tau) - ATT with standard errors and a uniform band, from the same bootstrap draws (ptetools 1.1.0, ptetools #27). Its p-value tests QTT(tau) = ATT at every tau: whether the effect is more than a location shift. See autoplot(res, type = "qtt_minus_att"). This includes panel_qtt()’s default long copula, which has its own aggregation.

  • New cdf_did() (and its workhorse cdf_did_gt()): the QTT and ATT under parallel trends in the distribution functions of untreated potential outcomes (Roth and Sant’Anna 2023), with staggered adoption, for panel data or repeated cross sections. The counterfactual distribution is computed exactly on the data’s support and rearranged into a valid distribution function; the ATT equals the usual DiD ATT. Unlike the rank- and quantile-based estimators, it is identified for discrete outcomes. Covariates enter through est_method = c("aipw", "ipw", "reg"): a doubly robust, an inverse-probability-weighted, and an outcome-regression (distribution regression) version of the conditional assumption (Sant’Anna and Zhao 2020).

  • The estimators now warn, once per call, when the outcome looks discrete: more than 10% of observations at one value, or at most 20 distinct values (#17). Quantile treatment effects usually require a continuous outcome: quantiles jump at mass points, rank-based identification only gives bounds, and bootstrap inference can be unreliable. The warning has class qte_discrete_outcome, the thresholds are the options qte.mass_point_tol and qte.discrete_n_unique, and the diagnostics are returned as outcome_discreteness. cic_gt() no longer warns about “extreme ranks” once per group-time cell and bootstrap draw.

  • The covariate-adjusted estimators gain cond_dist = c("qr", "dr"): cic(), qdid(), ddid(), panel_qtt() (and their *_gt() workhorses), and the outcome-regression and AIPW branches of lou_qtt() and unc_qte(). With covariates, "dr" estimates conditional outcome distributions by distribution regression (a logit of 1{Y <= y} on the covariates at a grid of thresholds) instead of quantile regression. It handles outcomes with mass points (e.g. many zeros) naturally and avoids truncating each unit’s conditional distribution at its 1st and 99th percentiles. The default stays "qr", and the "qr" results are unchanged.

Bug fixes (these change results)

  • When a treated unit’s covariates aren’t spanned by the comparison group (e.g. a dummy for a region with treated units only), the conditional outcome models extrapolate. With cond_dist = "dr" this happened silently: the dummy got a zero coefficient, so those treated units got the reference category’s conditional distribution. With cond_dist = "qr" the estimators stopped with an uninformative Singular design matrix. Both now drop such columns and warn once per call, naming the covariates, the group-time cells and the (weighted) share of treated units affected (#16). This applies to every estimator with covariates, including mdid(), cdf_did() and unc_qte(). Dropped columns that don’t matter (a factor level no unit in the cell has, a duplicated covariate) give no warning, and covariates with full support give the same results as before. Use ptetools::check_overlap() for overlap diagnostics by cell.

  • Factor covariates (and factor() or character terms in xformula) with a level that the comparison group lacks in some cell no longer stop the covariate-adjusted estimators with a “new levels” error.

  • With panel data and covariates that change over time, the estimators now condition on each unit’s covariates from the base period of each group-time cell, as ptetools and did do. Before, cic(), qdid(), mdid() and cdf_did() fit the comparison group’s post-period distribution on post-period covariates, and lou_qtt() conditioned on covariates measured after treatment. panel_qtt() now fixes covariates at the earliest period each cell uses; it previously mixed two pre-treatment periods. Results with time-invariant covariates, and with repeated cross sections, are unchanged.

  • unc_qte()’s uniform confidence band could be absurdly wide (by orders of magnitude) when a requested quantile fell inside a mass point of the outcome, such as zero earnings. The critical value standardized each quantile’s bootstrap draws by an IQR-based scale, which is nearly 0 there, while the band used the standard deviation. The draws are now standardized by the same standard deviation the band uses, and quantiles whose draws never vary are left out of the critical value, as the panel estimators do (ptetools 1.1.0, ptetools #33). Standard errors are unchanged; uniform bands change.

  • With more than one treated cohort, the aggregated QTTs (overall, event study and group) mixed the wrong group-time cells, including pre-treatment ones. The aggregation weights were in a different order from the cells they were applied to. Fixed in ptetools 1.1.0, which qte now requires. This affected cic(), qdid(), ddid(), mdid(), lou_qtt() and panel_qtt(pre_copula = "short") with gt_type = "qtt" or "qott"; ATTs were not affected, and neither was panel_qtt()’s default pre_copula = "long", whose aggregation is in qte. On the package’s test data the median QTT moves by up to 0.13, toward the true effect.

  • Fixed covariate-adjusted cic(), qdid(), ddid() and panel_qtt() (and their *_gt() workhorses) (#9):

    • They no longer fail when a group has a single treated unit.
    • Conditional quantiles are now rearranged (sorted) before use, so the conditional CDFs are monotone when quantile regressions cross.
    • Conditional ranks are no longer one quantile-grid step (0.01) too low. This came from quantreg’s predict(..., type = "Fhat", stepfun = TRUE) and biased the counterfactual distribution downward.
    • Conditional CDFs and quantile functions are now linearly interpolated between the estimated quantiles, not step functions, so ranks are no longer rounded down to the quantile grid. Beyond the first and last estimated quantiles they stay flat (no tail extrapolation).

    Covariate-adjusted estimates change as a result. In a simulation where conditional CiC holds exactly, the bias of the ATT falls from 0.15 to 0.02. Estimates without covariates are unchanged.

  • ddid() / ddid_gt() with covariates now integrate the counterfactual over the treated group’s covariate distribution, by reweighting control units with the propensity-score odds p(X)/(1 - p(X)) (#10). Previously the controls’ covariate distribution was used, which biased the ATT and QTT whenever treatment depends on the covariates (bias 0.84 in a simple simulated design; now about 0). Results without covariates are unchanged.

  • est_method = "aipw" in unc_qte() and lou_qtt() now reports a doubly-robust ATT/ATE: the mean of the AIPW counterfactual distribution, using the outcome model’s conditional mean (#11). Previously the reported ATT/ATE was the IPW estimate, so it ignored the outcome model and wasn’t doubly robust. The AIPW quantile curves are unchanged.

  • unc_qte()‘s cband = TRUE (the default) now reports a uniform confidence band, qte +/- c * qte.se, built the same way as the panel estimators’ uniform bands. Previously cband was ignored: qte.lower / qte.upper were always pointwise intervals, though summary() labelled them “Simult.”. The bootstrap critical value c was already computed and stored. Bands are typically wider under the default; use cband = FALSE for pointwise intervals. summary() and autoplot() label and draw the band correctly, including for QTE objects saved by earlier versions.

  • unc_qte() with weightsname: each bootstrap draw now resamples units together with their weights. Previously the weights stayed in their original row order while the rows were resampled, so standard errors and confidence bands with weights were wrong. Point estimates are unchanged.

  • unc_qte() now uses weightsname throughout: in the propensity-score model, in the outcome-regression fits, and in the AIPW distribution functions (previously only in the final averaging). lou_qtt()’s propensity-score model is now weighted too. With integer weights, the estimates now equal those from the unweighted fit on row-replicated data. Results without weights are unchanged.

  • With groups and time periods coded as calendar years, naming the group column G or the time column period gave NaN estimates (ptetools #13). Fixed in ptetools, which now keeps its internal columns separate from the user’s; panel_qtt()’s subset function uses those internal columns. Requires ptetools (>= 1.1.0). Results for other column names are unchanged.

  • panel_qtt() now treats anticipation in units of the time variable, as did::att_gt() and ptetools do: a cell is post-treatment from g - anticipation on, pre1 is the last period at least anticipation before g, and not-yet-treated comparison units must not be treated or anticipating treatment by the cell’s latest period. It previously counted anticipation in periods and ignored it for the comparison group. Results without anticipation are unchanged.

  • panel_qtt(gt_type = "qtt") with the default pre_copula = "long" no longer fails (“no valid post-treatment cells”) or drops valid cells when time periods are unequally spaced, e.g. lalonde.psid.panel (1974, 1975, 1978). The aggregation step checked whether the earlier base period exists in calendar years, while the estimator chooses base periods by position in the panel. Results with equally spaced periods are unchanged.

  • With weightsname, the panel estimators’ overall and event-study results (ATT and QTT) now combine cohorts by their weighted shares, as did does. They used unweighted counts of units, so results were wrong whenever the average weight differed across cohorts (ptetools #23; for panel_qtt(pre_copula = "long"), which aggregates in qte, #13). Integer weights now give the same estimates as duplicating units. Results without weights are unchanged.

  • mdid() with covariates no longer fails with “object ‘pre_ctrl’ not found”. The outcome regressions looked up their weights where lm() could not see them, so mdid() errored for any non-empty xformula.

Minor improvements

  • msm is no longer a suggested package; nothing used it.
  • Aggregated QTTs are now computed exactly: the group-time cells’ CDFs are mixed from every support point and the mixture inverted exactly, instead of on a 1,000-point grid of the pooled outcome (#19; ptetools #25 for the estimators that use ptetools’ aggregation, and panel_qtt()’s long-copula aggregation in qte). QTT estimates change slightly (by a few thousandths on the package’s tests and mpdta), and weighted data now gives the same QTTs as the equivalent row-replicated data. Requires BMisc (>= 1.4.11).
  • unc_qte() now checks up front that dname is a column of data coded 0/1, with an informative error. A treatment coded e.g. 1/2 previously failed inside the propensity-score fit with “y values must be 0 <= y <= 1” (#1).
  • unc_qte() drops rows with missing values in the outcome, treatment, weights or covariates (with a warning) instead of failing. Its internals were rewritten as standalone code; results without weights are unchanged.
  • cic() and qdid() with covariates and weightsname (panel data): the ATT paired the counterfactual outcomes, sorted by unit id, with weights in data row order (#14). ptetools sorts panel data by id, so results were not affected in practice; the ATT now uses the same id-ordered weights as the counterfactual distribution.
  • Invalid sampling weights in the panel estimators (missing, negative, or varying over time within a unit) now give a clear error, from ptetools (#24), instead of NaN or silently inconsistent estimates.
  • Repeated cross sections (#18): the help pages and README now say which estimators accept panel = FALSE (cic(), qdid(), mdid(), cdf_did(), and lou_qtt() with lagged_outcome_cov = FALSE) and why ddid() and panel_qtt() need panel data. New tests check that, on panel data, panel = FALSE gives the panel estimates, and that the estimators work on genuine repeated cross sections.
  • New tests check that integer weights match row replication for every panel estimator, and that rescaling the weights changes nothing (#15).
  • unc_qte()’s pscore.reg no longer carries copies of the data. The fit kept the estimator’s working data twice over, through $data/$model and through its formula’s environment, so a saved QTE object for lalonde.psid shrinks from about 3.6 MB to 0.4 MB. coef(), vcov(), summary(), fitted() and predict(newdata = ) are unchanged; anova() and update(), which refit the model, no longer work on it.

Performance

  • cic(), qdid(), ddid(), mdid(), panel_qtt() and lou_qtt() are faster, with the same results:
    • Weighted ranks and quantiles in the *_gt() functions use one sort instead of a pass over the data for each unit, so they are no longer quadratic in the group size.
    • The covariate versions of cic() and qdid() fit the post-period quantile regression for the comparison group once per period, not once per cohort, because it is the same for every cohort already treated by that period.
    • Only the columns the estimators use are passed to ptetools::pte().
    Combined with the faster empirical bootstrap in ptetools 1.1.0, unconditional CiC on a 3,000-unit, 30-period panel runs more than 20 times faster.

qte 2.0.0

CRAN release: 2026-07-23

This is a major update that extends all estimators to support staggered treatment adoption. The API has changed substantially — please read this section before upgrading.

New functions

  • unc_qte() — cross-sectional QTE and QTT under unconfoundedness. Supports IPW, outcome regression, and doubly robust (AIPW) estimation. Uses a yname/dname interface consistent with the did/ptetools convention. Replaces ci.qte() and ci.qtet(), which are retained as deprecated wrappers.

  • cic() / cic_gt() — Change in Changes estimator for staggered treatment adoption (Athey and Imbens 2006). Supports panel and repeated cross sections data, and returns either ATT (gt_type = "att") or a full QTT curve (gt_type = "qtt"). Replaces CiC(), which is retained as a deprecated wrapper.

  • qdid() / qdid_gt() — Quantile Difference in Differences estimator for staggered treatment adoption (Callaway, Li, and Oka 2018). Replaces QDiD(), which is retained as a deprecated wrapper.

  • mdid() / mdid_gt() — Mean Difference in Differences estimator for staggered treatment adoption (Callaway and Li 2019). Replaces MDiD(), which is retained as a deprecated wrapper.

  • ddid() / ddid_gt() — Distributional Difference in Differences estimator for staggered treatment adoption (Callaway and Li 2019). Replaces ddid2(), which is retained as a deprecated wrapper.

  • panel_qtt() / panel_qtt_gt() — Panel QTT estimator using copula transfer across pre-treatment periods (Callaway and Li 2019), with staggered treatment adoption support. The pre_copula argument controls whether a rolling ("long", default) or fixed ("short") base period is used to transfer the copula. Replaces panel.qtet(), which is retained as a deprecated wrapper.

  • lou_qtt() — Lagged-outcome unconfoundedness QTT estimator for staggered treatment adoption. Uses the lagged outcome as a control variable to identify the QTT. New; no prior equivalent in the package.

Deprecated functions

The following functions emit a runtime deprecation warning via .Deprecated() and will be removed in v2.1 (target: 2026-08). Each points to its modern replacement in the warning message.

Deprecated Replacement
ci.qte() unc_qte(target = "qte")
ci.qtet() unc_qte(target = "qtt")
CiC() cic()
QDiD() qdid()
MDiD() mdid()
ddid2() ddid()
panel.qtet() panel_qtt()

Removed functions

  • computeDiffSE() — was dead code; never called anywhere in the package. Design notes for a future QTT-vs-ATT test are in dev/NOTES.md.

  • DR(), spatt(), bounds() — removed in earlier 1.5.x development work.

  • qtes2mat(), diffQ() — formatting helpers tied to the legacy QTE class with no internal callers.

Infrastructure

  • Full testthat test suite added (83 fast tests; 10 slow bootstrap tests skipped by default, enabled via R_SLOW_TESTS=true). The package previously had no tests.

  • All new estimators are backed by ptetools::pte(). The attgt_fun hook pattern makes it straightforward to add new identification strategies without duplicating bootstrap or aggregation code.

  • Estimators now pass an explicit aggte_fun to ptetools::pte(), replacing the earlier implicit dispatch based on gt_type.

  • ptetools added to Imports (was missing from DESCRIPTION despite being used).

  • Hmisc and texreg removed from Imports (were unused after earlier cleanup).

  • License updated from GPL-2 to GPL-3.

qte 1.4.0

  • Added cic2() for Change in Changes with multiple periods and variation in treatment timing, using ptetools as a backend. This function was experimental; it has been superseded by cic() in v2.0.0.

qte 1.3.3

  • Bug fix: critical values for uniform confidence bands now correctly reflect the alp argument rather than being stuck at alp = 0.05.

qte 1.3.2

  • Significance level is now passed through in the results.
  • Added ability to change significance level in ggqte() for pointwise confidence intervals without re-estimating.

qte 1.3.1

CRAN release: 2022-09-01

  • Updated maintainer contact information.
  • Improvements and updates to vignettes.

qte 1.3.0

CRAN release: 2019-06-10

  • Added first-step quantile regression support for panel.qtet(), QDiD(), and CiC().
  • Added checks that input data is in the correct format, particularly for panel data.

qte 1.2.3

  • Now using empirical quantiles in the CiC method.
  • Added code for computing uniform confidence bands.
  • General improvements to the codebase, including combining shared code across methods.

qte 1.2.2

CRAN release: 2018-04-30

  • Bug fixes to the CiC method.

qte 1.2

  • Added ddid2() to compute quantile treatment effects under a Difference in Differences assumption following Callaway and Li (2016).
  • Covariates for all methods now specified using formulas (xformla argument) rather than passing variable names directly.
  • Improvements to bootstrapping standard errors.
  • Some extensions to computing the ATT via spatt().
  • Preliminary version of multi-period ATT moved to the did package.
